title: Safely managed drinking water, SDG regions compared
headline: Safely managed water for all by 2030 needs a rise of 11.4 points a year in Sub-Saharan Africa
subtitle: Proportion of the population using drinking water from an improved source that is accessible on premises, available when needed and free from contamination
years: In Sub-Saharan Africa it has risen 0.6 points a year, from 17.4% in 2000 to 31.7% in 2024.
data_line: Data: WHO/UNICEF JMP via UN SDG Global Database, series SH_H2O_SAFE, extracted 1 Nov 2026
alt: Safely managed water for all by 2030 needs a rise of 11.4 points a year in Sub-Saharan Africa. In Sub-Saharan Africa it has risen 0.6 points a year, from 17.4% in 2000 to 31.7% in 2024. Sub-Saharan Africa: 0.6 a year observed, 11.4 needed; World: 0.5 a year observed, 4.4 needed; E. and S.-E. Asia: 0.3 a year observed, 4.1 needed; N. Africa and W. Asia: 0.4 a year observed, 4.0 needed; Central and S. Asia: 1.2 a year observed, 3.8 needed; Latin America, Caribbean: 0.4 a year observed, 3.5 needed; Europe and N. America: 0.1 a year observed, 1.0 needed
method: Method: linear pace on published aggregates, from 2000 for Sub-Saharan Africa.
question: Which countries in Sub-Saharan Africa have moved safely managed drinking water fastest, and how?
